subproblem.title: Linearity of g ↦ ∫_S div g on compactly supported C¹ vector fields
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set. Write div g(x) for the trace of the Fréchet derivative Dg(x) (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanDivergence) and ∫_S for the Lebesgue integral over S. (i) If g, h : ℝ^N → ℝ^N are C¹ with compact support, then ∫_S div(g + h) dL^N = ∫_S div g dL^N + ∫_S div h dL^N. (ii) If c ∈ ℝ and g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is C¹, then ∫_S div(c g) dL^N = c ∫_S div g dL^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn N)), (∀ g h : Rn N → Rn N, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → HasCompactSupport h → ∫ x in S, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence (g + h) x = (∫ x in S, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x) + ∫ x in S, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence h x) ∧ ∀ (c : ℝ) (g : Rn N → Rn N), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → ∫ x in S, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence (c • g) x = c * ∫ x in S, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 1 of the parent proof ("Λ₀(g) := ∫_{E∩U} div g; div g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable ... div(a g + b h) = a div g + b div h pointwise, by linearity of the derivative and of the trace"), stated for an arbitrary set S in place of E ∩ U; the argument uses no property of S. It underlies the remark after Simon Ch. 2, (2.1) (chapter-02.txt lines 480-498, printed p. 48).

Notation. div g(x) := trace(Dg(x)), where Dg(x) = fderiv ℝ g x (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanDivergence), and ∫_S is the Bochner integral for Lebesgue measure restricted to S. Fix an orthonormal basis b_1, …, b_N of ℝ^N (stdOrthonormalBasis). Then div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨b_i, Dg(x) b_i⟩ for every g and x (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence_eq_sum_inner).

1. Continuity. Let g be C¹. Then x ↦ Dg(x) is continuous into the continuous linear maps (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, with 1 ≠ 0). For each i, x ↦ Dg(x) b_i is continuous (evaluation at a fixed vector, Continuous.clm_apply), so x ↦ ⟨b_i, Dg(x) b_i⟩ is continuous. Hence div g, a finite sum of these (continuous_finsetSum), is continuous.

2. Support and integrability. For every g, div g(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ tsupport g (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset: support(div g) ⊆ tsupport g). If g has compact support, the support of div g lies in the compact set tsupport g, so div g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono'). If moreover g is C¹, then div g is continuous with compact support. It is therefore Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^N (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport) and hence integrable on S (Integrable.restrict).

3. Pointwise additivity. Let g, h be C¹ and x ∈ ℝ^N. Both maps are differentiable at x (ContDiff.differentiable, 1 ≠ 0), so D(g + h)(x) = Dg(x) + Dh(x) (fderiv_add). The trace is additive, so div(g + h)(x) = div g(x) + div h(x).

4. Proof of (i). Let g, h be C¹ with compact support. By step 3 the integrands agree pointwise, so ∫_S div(g + h) = ∫_S (div g + div h). By step 2, div g and div h are integrable on S, so additivity of the integral (integral_add) gives ∫_S (div g + div h) = ∫_S div g + ∫_S div h.

5. Pointwise homogeneity. Let g be C¹, c ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^N. Since g is differentiable at x, D(c g)(x) = c·Dg(x) (fderiv_const_smul). The trace is linear, so div(c g)(x) = c·div g(x).

6. Proof of (ii). By step 5, ∫_S div(c g) = ∫_S c·div g(x) dx. A constant factor comes out of a Bochner integral without any integrability hypothesis (integral_const_mul), so ∫_S c·div g = c ∫_S div g. ∎
proof_key_steps: For C¹ g, div g = Σ_i ⟨b_i, Dg(·) b_i⟩ is continuous; it vanishes off tsupport g, so it is integrable on S when g has compact support.
D(g + h) = Dg + Dh and D(c g) = c Dg for differentiable fields; the trace is linear, so div(g + h) = div g + div h and div(c g) = c div g pointwise.
Additivity of the integral for integrable integrands gives (i); pulling the constant out of the integral (no integrability needed) gives (ii).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches both prose clauses, including arbitrary S and no compact-support requirement for homogeneity. The proof establishes continuity and compact support of divergence, integrability under arbitrary restriction, derivative/trace linearity, and the required integral identities. Unconditional integral_const_mul justifies clause (ii). The argument is complete and independent; its bare declaration name is unreserved.
